description:
- Consider a rocket that travels along a straight path. 
- Let x_t, v_t, and a_t be the position, velocity, and acceleration, respectively, of the rocket at time t.
- By discretizing time and by taking the time increment to be unity, we obtain an approximate discrete-time model of the form 
    
    x_{t+1} = x_t + v_t
    v_{t+1} = v_t + a_t

- We assume that the acceleration a_t is under our control, as it is determined by the rocket thrust.
- In a rough model, the magnitude |a_t| of the accelera­tion can be assumed to be equal to the rate of fuel consumption at time t.
- Suppose that we have x_0 and v_0 as the initial position and velocity, respectively, of the rocket.
- We wish the rocket to take off and reach a target position x_T with speed v_T at time T.
- The goal is to achieve this with the least pressure on the passengers, minimizing the maximum thrust required.

FinalPosition.definition: Target final position of the rocket

FinalVelocity.definition: Target final velocity of the rocket

objective.description: "Minimize the maximum absolute acceleration (maximum thrust) over the entire time horizon in order to reduce the peak pressure on the passengers."

constraints.description: For all time steps t = 0, ..., TotalTime - 1: x_{t+1} = x_t + v_t
For all time steps t = 0, ..., TotalTime - 1: v_{t+1} = v_t + a_t
